title: What 'take your Boston' means
summary: Waters explains that taking a 'Boston' meant a chorus played with a back beat on two and four, though he does not know where the name came from.

story.theme_name: Drummers and drumming: who played what, and how
story.community_name: Great drummers: who they admired and why

blocks.x: Let me ask you a question about Boston since, there's a phrase from the early days of hot jazz called "take your Boston".

Yes, right, now, now. Yeah, now here's what this Boston is. This Boston, it specifies, see. It don't mean "take a chorus"; it means take a chorus, but it, the, but the type of rhythm is specified. When you play a Boston - you hear some of these Dixieland bands doin' it now - everybody has a back beat, like this (claps 2 and 4), everybody, you know? Even the drums, everybody has that back beat. Instead of saying "Um chuck chuck chuck chuck chuck", they'd say, everybody (claps and sings back beat), see, that's the Boston. And that's the way they used to take Bostons in that period.
Do you have any idea of why it called "take your Boston?"
I never did an idea of how the Boston came in. Now that I don't know at all. I would like to find out where did they get that name from, unless - I don't know, I don't know, see.
Did they used that expression "take your Boston" -
Yeah. Yeah, but they use it in New York, too.
Everywhere, but also in Boston, they'd even say "take your Boston" in Boston?
Yeah, they was takin' their things, and the Boston was like this, afterbeat (claps back beat), somethin' like that - what's that new -
What I'm asking specifically is did they used the expression "take your Boston" for that kind of solo you just described in Boston, Massachusetts -

Yeah, sure. They use it there, too. You know, not everybody 'cause everybody isn't the same, understand what I mean, see. They had groups up there to dance to. See, they had all different kinds of groups, you know, in Boston just like they had different kinds of groups all over, see. One band wouldn't ever do that, where another one would. (end of reel 2)
